source.text: וַ֠יִּסְעוּ כָּל־עֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֛ין לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel from [the] wilderness of Sin by their stages, on [the] mouth of Yahweh, and they encamped at Rephidim, and there [was] not water to drink [for] the people.

en.L: And all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin by their stages, at the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they camped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
en.B: The whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} moved on from the wilderness of Sin, traveling in stages as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded. They made camp at Rephidim, but there was no water there for the people to drink.
en.R: The whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left the Desert of Sin. They traveled from place to place, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them. They set up camp at Rephidim, but there was no water there for the people to drink.

es.L: Y partió toda la comunidad de los hijos de Israel del desierto de Sin, por sus etapas, conforme a la orden {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y acamparon en Refidim, y no había agua para que bebiera el pueblo.
es.B: Toda la comunidad de los israelitas partió del desierto de Sin, avanzando por etapas según lo ordenaba {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Acamparon en Refidim, pero allí no había agua para que el pueblo bebiera.
es.R: Toda la comunidad de los israelitas salió del desierto de Sin. Viajaban de un lugar a otro, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les decía. Pusieron su campamento en Refidim, pero allí no había agua para que la gente bebiera.

fr.L: Et toute la communauté des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël partit du désert de Sin, selon ses étapes, sur l’ordre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et ils campèrent à Rephidim, et il n’y avait pas d’eau à boire pour le peuple.
fr.B: Toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} quitta le désert de Sin, voyageant d’étape en étape comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’ordonnait. Ils dressèrent le camp à Rephidim, mais il n’y avait pas d’eau à boire pour le peuple.
fr.R: Toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} a quitté le désert de Sin. Ils ont voyagé d’un endroit à l’autre, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le leur disait. Ils ont installé leur camp à Rephidim, mais là, il n’y avait pas d’eau à boire pour le peuple.

sw.L: Nayo jumuiya yote ya wana wa Israeli ikasafiri kutoka jangwa la Sini, kwa safari zao, kwa amri ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakapiga kambi Refidimu, wala hapakuwa na maji ya kunywa kwa ajili ya watu.
sw.B: Jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli iliondoka katika jangwa la Sini, ikisafiri hatua kwa hatua kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoagiza. Walipiga kambi Refidimu, lakini hapakuwa na maji ya kunywa kwa ajili ya watu.
sw.R: Jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli iliondoka katika jangwa la Sini. Walisafiri kutoka mahali hadi mahali, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyowaambia. Walipiga kambi Refidimu, lakini hapakuwa na maji ya kunywa huko.

vi.L: Cả hội chúng con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên ra đi từ hoang mạc Sin theo từng chặng đường của họ, theo lệnh [từ] miệng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và họ đóng trại tại Rê-phi-đim; và không có nước cho dân uống.
vi.B: Cả hội chúng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên rời hoang mạc Sin, đi từng chặng theo lệnh của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ đóng trại tại Rê-phi-đim, nhưng ở đó không có nước cho dân uống.
vi.R: Toàn thể dân Y-sơ-ra-ên rời hoang mạc Sin. Họ đi từ nơi này đến nơi khác, theo lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chỉ dẫn. Họ dựng trại tại Rê-phi-đim, nhưng ở đó không có nước cho dân uống.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 자손의 온 회중이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 입대로 그들의 여정을 따라 신 광야를 떠나 르비딤에 진을 쳤다. 그런데 백성이 마실 물이 없었다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 백성의 온 회중은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 명령하신 대로 한 곳씩 옮겨 가며 신 광야를 떠났다. 그들은 르비딤에 진을 쳤으나, 그곳에는 백성이 마실 물이 없었다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 사람들은 모두 신 광야를 떠났다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하시는 대로 이곳저곳으로 옮겨 다녔다. 그들이 르비딤에 진을 쳤는데, 그곳에는 백성이 마실 물이 없었다.

pt.L: E toda a comunidade dos filhos de Israel partiu do deserto de Sim, segundo as suas etapas, conforme a boca {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e acamparam em Refidim, e não havia água para o povo beber.
pt.B: Toda a comunidade dos israelitas partiu do deserto de Sim, viajando por etapas, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ordenava. Eles acamparam em Refidim, mas ali não havia água para o povo beber.
pt.R: Toda a comunidade dos israelitas saiu do deserto de Sim. Eles foram viajando de um lugar para outro, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhes dizia. Montaram acampamento em Refidim, mas ali não havia água para o povo beber.

decisions.choice: on the mouth of Yahweh: at Yahweh's command
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says, so to move "on the mouth" of the LORD is to move at his word (Numbers 9:18-23). The cloud led their journeys (13:21-22).

decisions.choice: by their stages: one camp after another
decisions.reason: The word is used of the moves from one camping place to the next (Numbers 33:1-2). Numbers 33:12-14 names two camps, Dophkah and Alush, between the wilderness of Sin and Rephidim.

decisions.choice: Rephidim: a camp on the way to Sinai
decisions.reason: Rephidim is the last camp before Mount Sinai (19:2; Numbers 33:14-15). Its exact place is not known.

decisions.choice: "conforme a la orden del SEÑOR" for "on the mouth of Yahweh" at Literal
decisions.reason: Spanish does not use "boca" for a command in this way, so Literal gives the sense, as the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("partit", "campèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("a quitté"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level.

decisions.choice: "sur l'ordre du SEIGNEUR" for "on the mouth of Yahweh" at Literal
decisions.reason: French cannot use "bouche" for what someone commands; a word-for-word "sur la bouche" would mean a kiss. "Sur l'ordre" gives the sense the meaning decision states.

decisions.choice: "kwa amri ya BWANA" for "on the mouth of Yahweh" at Literal
decisions.reason: "Kwa kinywa cha" would suggest that the LORD spoke the words aloud to them, not that they moved at his command; Literal gives the sense of the idiom.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (L), "이스라엘 백성" (B), "이스라엘 사람들" (R) for "the sons of Israel"
alternatives: a gender span, as in the English
decisions.reason: The Korean words already include women and men, so Korean needs no gender span where the English has one; the three forms follow the Exodus-Deuteronomy term sheet and are used through these chapters.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, with the particle outside the span
decisions.reason: The divine name is the setting span of the Korean Old Testament (주 by default, 야훼 as the alternative), at every level; both forms end in a vowel, so one particle (께서, 의, 를) fits both. The older Protestant form "여호와" is not used.

decisions.choice: "회중" for the congregation, "진을 치다" for making camp
decisions.reason: The term sheet's words for these books, so the congregation and the camp read the same through Exodus to Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L); "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The term sheet for Exodus to Deuteronomy gives these forms for "the sons of Israel". Vietnamese "con cháu" and "dân" already take in men and women, so there is only one form and nothing for the English gender setting to switch; the same holds through these chapters.

decisions.choice: "hội chúng" for the congregation; "hoang mạc" for the wilderness
decisions.reason: The forms the term sheet sets for the whole Pentateuch, recorded once for chapters 17 to 24. Readable drops "hội chúng" for "toàn thể dân", the plain word, as the English Readable says "the whole community".

decisions.choice: Refidim
decisions.reason: For the whole book, where the name first appears: "Refidim", with "f" for ph and the final -im Portuguese keeps from the Hebrew plural, as in "querubim".

source.text: וַיָּ֤רֶב הָעָם֙ עִם־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ תְּנוּ־לָ֥נוּ מַ֖יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה מַה־תְּרִיבוּן֙ עִמָּדִ֔י מַה־תְּנַסּ֖וּן אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And quarreled the people with Moses, and they said, give to us water that we may drink. And said to them Moses, why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahweh?

en.L: And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said, "Give us water, that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"
en.B: The people turned on Moses in a quarrel. "Give us water to drink!" they demanded. Moses answered them, "Why pick a quarrel with me? Why put {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the test?"
en.R: The people argued with Moses. "Give us water to drink!" they shouted. Moses answered, "Why are you arguing with me? Why are you testing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"

es.L: Y contendió el pueblo con Moisés, y dijeron: «{{plural_you:Dennos|Dadnos}} agua para que bebamos». Y les dijo Moisés: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:contienden|contendéis}} conmigo? ¿Por qué {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}?».
es.B: El pueblo se enfrentó a Moisés en una disputa. «¡{{plural_you:Dennos|Dadnos}} agua para beber!», le exigían. Moisés les respondió: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:pelean|peleáis}} conmigo? ¿Por qué {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}?».
es.R: El pueblo discutió con Moisés. «¡{{plural_you:Dennos|Dadnos}} agua para beber!», gritaban. Moisés les contestó: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:discuten|discutís}} conmigo? ¿Por qué {{plural_you:están poniendo|estáis poniendo}} a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}?».

fr.L: Et le peuple chercha querelle à Moïse, et ils dirent : « Donnez-nous de l’eau, pour que nous buvions. » Et Moïse leur dit : « Pourquoi me cherchez-vous querelle ? Pourquoi mettez-vous à l’épreuve {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? »
fr.B: Le peuple s’en prit à Moïse et lui chercha querelle. « Donnez-nous de l’eau à boire ! » exigèrent-ils. Moïse leur répondit : « Pourquoi me chercher querelle ? Pourquoi mettre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à l’épreuve ? »
fr.R: Le peuple s’est disputé avec Moïse. « Donnez-nous de l’eau à boire ! » criaient-ils. Moïse leur a répondu : « Pourquoi vous disputez-vous avec moi ? Pourquoi mettez-vous {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à l’épreuve ? »

sw.L: Nao watu wakagombana na Musa, wakasema, "Tupeni maji tunywe." Naye Musa akawaambia, "Mbona mnagombana nami? Mbona mnamjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?"
sw.B: Watu walimgeukia Musa wakagombana naye. "Tupeni maji ya kunywa!" wakadai. Musa akawajibu, "Kwa nini mnaanzisha ugomvi nami? Kwa nini mnamjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?"
sw.R: Watu walibishana na Musa. "Tupeni maji ya kunywa!" walipiga kelele. Musa akawajibu, "Kwa nini mnabishana nami? Kwa nini mnamjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?"

vi.L: Và dân cãi vã với Môi-se, và họ nói: "Hãy cho chúng tôi nước để chúng tôi uống." Và Môi-se nói với họ: "Sao các ngươi cãi vã với tôi? Sao các ngươi thử {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?"
vi.B: Dân chúng gây sự với Môi-se và đòi: "Hãy cho chúng tôi nước uống!" Môi-se đáp: "Sao anh em gây sự với tôi? Sao anh em lại thử thách {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?"
vi.R: Dân chúng cãi lẫy với Môi-se. Họ la lên: "Hãy cho chúng tôi nước uống!" Môi-se trả lời: "Sao anh em cãi lẫy với tôi? Sao anh em thử thách {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}?"

ko.L: 그러자 백성이 모세와 다투며 말했다. "우리에게 물을 주어 우리가 마시게 하십시오." 모세가 그들에게 말했다. "너희가 어찌하여 나와 다투느냐? 어찌하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 시험하느냐?"
ko.B: 백성은 모세에게 따지며 "마실 물을 내놓으십시오!" 하고 요구했다. 모세가 그들에게 대답했다. "너희는 왜 나에게 시비를 거느냐? 왜 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 시험하느냐?"
ko.R: 백성이 모세와 말다툼을 벌였다. "마실 물을 주십시오!" 하고 그들이 소리쳤다. 모세가 대답했다. "여러분은 왜 저와 다툽니까? 왜 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 시험합니까?"

pt.L: E o povo contendeu com Moisés, e disseram: "Deem-nos água para bebermos." E Moisés lhes disse: "Por que vocês contendem comigo? Por que põem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} à prova?"
pt.B: O povo entrou em disputa com Moisés. "Deem-nos água para beber!", exigiram. Moisés lhes respondeu: "Por que vocês brigam comigo? Por que põem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} à prova?"
pt.R: O povo discutiu com Moisés. "Deem-nos água para beber!", gritavam. Moisés respondeu: "Por que vocês estão discutindo comigo? Por que estão pondo {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} à prova?"

decisions.choice: quarrel: bring a complaint against, contend with
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a dispute or a legal complaint. The people are not only grumbling; they are making a case against Moses. The same root gives the name Meribah (verse 7).

decisions.choice: test: put to the proof, try whether God will act
decisions.reason: To test God is to demand that he prove himself, as though his care could not be trusted (Deuteronomy 6:16; Psalm 78:18-20). The same root gives the name Massah (verse 7).

decisions.choice: argued
decisions.reason: Readable says "argued", a common word for the same dispute. Literal and Balanced keep "quarrel", which carries the link to Meribah.

decisions.choice: "Tupeni" (plural): the people speak to more than Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is plural though Moses alone is named, so it takes in Aaron too, as in 16:3. Swahili shows the plural in the verb, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: The people call themselves "chúng tôi"; Moses calls them "các ngươi" (L), "anh em" (B, R) and himself "tôi"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's address forms for Moses and the people: "anh em" and "tôi" for Moses speaking to Israel at Balanced and Readable, "các ngươi" at Literal where the English Literal keeps the plain "you"; the people say "ông" and "chúng tôi" to Moses. Recorded once for these chapters.

decisions.choice: "thử" (L); "thử thách" (B, R)
decisions.reason: To put God to the proof (meaning decision), as in Genesis 22:1; "cám dỗ" would mean tempting to sin.

decisions.choice: The people speak to Moses in 합쇼체; Moses answers the people in 해라체 with "너희" (L, B) and in 합쇼체 with "여러분", calling himself "저" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean must choose a speech level. The term sheet for Exodus to Deuteronomy sets these forms for the people and their leader, and they hold through these chapters.

decisions.choice: contender (L); disputa (B); discutir (R); pôr à prova
decisions.reason: The two verbs give the names of verse 7 (m1, m2), so each level uses the same words there: "contender" and "disputa" for the quarrel, "pôr à prova" for the testing. "Tentar o SENHOR" is the older wording, but in Portuguese "tentar" now means to try or to tempt.

source.text: וַיִּצְמָ֨א שָׁ֤ם הָעָם֙ לַמַּ֔יִם וַיָּ֥לֶן הָעָ֖ם עַל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ הֶעֱלִיתָ֣נוּ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לְהָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֛י וְאֶת־בָּנַ֥י וְאֶת־מִקְנַ֖י בַּצָּמָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And thirsted there the people for water, and grumbled the people against Moses, and said, why this [have] you brought us up from Egypt to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?

en.L: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, "Why [is] this, [that] you brought us up from Egypt to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?"
en.B: But the people were thirsty there, and they grumbled against Moses. "Why did you ever bring us up out of Egypt?" they said. "Was it to make us die of thirst, with our children and our animals?"
en.R: But the people were very thirsty, and they complained to Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt? Did you want us and our children and our animals to die of thirst?"

es.L: Y tuvo sed allí el pueblo de agua, y murmuró el pueblo contra Moisés, y dijo: «¿Por qué [es] esto, [que] nos hiciste subir de Egipto para matarme de sed a mí, a mis hijos y a mi ganado?».
es.B: Pero el pueblo tenía sed allí, y murmuraron contra Moisés. «¿Por qué nos sacaste de Egipto?», decían. «¿Fue para hacernos morir de sed junto con nuestros hijos y nuestros animales?».
es.R: Pero el pueblo tenía mucha sed, y se quejaron con Moisés. Le dijeron: «¿Por qué nos sacaste de Egipto? ¿Querías que nosotros, nuestros hijos y nuestros animales muriéramos de sed?».

fr.L: Et le peuple eut soif d’eau là, et le peuple murmura contre Moïse, et il dit : « Pourquoi donc nous as-tu fait monter d’Égypte, pour me faire mourir de soif, moi, mes enfants et mon bétail ? »
fr.B: Mais le peuple avait soif en ce lieu, et il murmura contre Moïse. « Pourquoi nous as-tu fait monter d’Égypte ? disaient-ils. Était-ce pour nous faire mourir de soif, avec nos enfants et nos bêtes ? »
fr.R: Mais le peuple avait très soif, et les gens se sont plaints à Moïse. Ils disaient : « Pourquoi nous as-tu fait sortir d’Égypte ? Tu voulais nous faire mourir de soif, nous, nos enfants et nos animaux ? »

sw.L: Nao watu wakaona kiu ya maji huko, nao watu wakamnung'unikia Musa, wakasema, "Mbona hivi, umetupandisha kutoka Misri ili kuniua mimi na watoto wangu na mifugo yangu kwa kiu?"
sw.B: Lakini watu waliona kiu huko, wakamnung'unikia Musa. "Kwa nini ulitutoa Misri?" walisema. "Je, ni ili tufe kwa kiu pamoja na watoto wetu na wanyama wetu?"
sw.R: Lakini watu walikuwa na kiu sana, wakamlalamikia Musa. Walisema, "Kwa nini ulitutoa Misri? Je, ulitaka sisi, watoto wetu na wanyama wetu tufe kwa kiu?"

vi.L: Và dân khát nước tại đó, và dân lằm bằm nghịch cùng Môi-se và nói: "Sao vậy, [mà] ông đã đem chúng tôi lên khỏi Ai Cập để giết tôi, con cái tôi và súc vật tôi bằng cơn khát?"
vi.B: Nhưng dân chúng khát nước ở đó, và họ lằm bằm chống lại Môi-se. Họ nói: "Ông đem chúng tôi lên khỏi Ai Cập làm gì? Có phải để cho chúng tôi, con cái và súc vật chúng tôi chết khát không?"
vi.R: Nhưng dân chúng rất khát, và họ phàn nàn với Môi-se. Họ nói: "Sao ông đem chúng tôi ra khỏi Ai Cập? Ông muốn chúng tôi, con cái chúng tôi và súc vật chúng tôi chết khát hay sao?"

ko.L: 그러나 백성이 거기서 물 때문에 목이 말랐고, 백성이 모세에게 원망하며 말했다. "어찌하여 이렇게, 당신은 우리를 이집트에서 올라오게 하여 나와 내 자식들과 내 가축을 목말라 죽게 하십니까?"
ko.B: 그러나 백성은 그곳에서 목이 말라 모세에게 불평했다. "왜 당신은 우리를 이집트에서 데리고 나왔습니까? 우리와 우리 자식들과 가축을 목말라 죽게 하려는 것입니까?"
ko.R: 그러나 백성은 몹시 목이 말라서 모세에게 불평했다. "왜 우리를 이집트에서 데리고 나왔습니까? 우리와 우리 아이들과 짐승들을 목말라 죽게 하려고 그랬습니까?"

pt.L: E o povo teve sede ali de água, e o povo murmurou contra Moisés e disse: "Por que [é] isso, [que] você nos fez subir do Egito para me matar de sede, a mim, aos meus filhos e ao meu gado?"
pt.B: Mas o povo tinha sede ali e reclamou contra Moisés. "Por que você nos tirou do Egito?", diziam. "Foi para nos fazer morrer de sede, com os nossos filhos e os nossos animais?"
pt.R: Mas o povo estava com muita sede e reclamou com Moisés. Eles disseram: "Por que você nos tirou do Egito? Você queria que nós, os nossos filhos e os nossos animais morrêssemos de sede?"

decisions.choice: me ... my children ... my livestock: the people speak as one
decisions.reason: The people are spoken of as one body, so they say "me" and "my". The words mean all of them, with their children and herds.

decisions.choice: grumbled: the complaint of the wilderness years
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the grumbling at Marah (15:24) and over food (16:2, 7-8). Moses says there that it is really against the LORD (16:8).

decisions.choice: us ... our
decisions.reason: English does not let a crowd say "me", so Balanced and Readable say "us" and "our". Literal keeps "me" and "my".

decisions.choice: "원망하다" (L); "불평하다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The grumbling of the wilderness years: "원망하다" keeps the weight of the complaint against Moses and God at Literal; "불평하다" is the plain modern word.

decisions.choice: "tôi ... con cái tôi ... súc vật tôi" (L); "chúng tôi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The people speak as one person (meaning decision); Literal keeps the singular, Balanced and Readable say "chúng tôi", as the English does.

source.text: וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה ע֥וֹד מְעַ֖ט וּסְקָלֻֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And cried out Moses to Yahweh, saying, what will I do with this people? Yet a little and they will stone me.

en.L: And Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "What shall I do with this people? Yet a little and they will stone me."
en.B: Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "What am I going to do with this people? A little more of this, and they will stone me!"
en.R: Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. "What should I do with these people?" he said. "Soon they will be throwing stones at me to kill me!"

es.L: Y clamó Moisés {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «¿Qué haré con este pueblo? Un poco más y me apedrearán».
es.B: Moisés clamó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Qué voy a hacer con este pueblo? ¡Un poco más de esto y me matarán a pedradas!».
es.R: Moisés le pidió ayuda a gritos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. «¿Qué debo hacer con esta gente?», le dijo. «¡Muy pronto me van a tirar piedras para matarme!».

fr.L: Et Moïse cria vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en disant : « Que ferai-je avec ce peuple ? Encore un peu, et ils me lapideront. »
fr.B: Moïse cria {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Que vais-je faire de ce peuple ? Encore un peu, et ils vont me lapider ! »
fr.R: Moïse a appelé {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au secours. « Que dois-je faire avec ces gens ? a-t-il dit. Bientôt, ils vont me jeter des pierres pour me tuer ! »

sw.L: Naye Musa akamlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akisema, "Nitawafanyaje watu hawa? Bado kidogo nao watanipiga kwa mawe."
sw.B: Musa alimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Nifanye nini na watu hawa? Hali hii ikiendelea kidogo tu, watanipiga mawe!"
sw.R: Musa alimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Nifanye nini na watu hawa? Muda si mrefu watanirushia mawe ili kuniua!"

vi.L: Và Môi-se kêu cầu cùng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Con sẽ làm gì với dân này? Còn một chút nữa thôi là họ sẽ ném đá con."
vi.B: Môi-se kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con phải làm gì với dân này đây? Chỉ chút nữa thôi là họ ném đá con!"
vi.R: Môi-se kêu cầu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con phải làm gì với những người này? Chẳng bao lâu nữa họ sẽ ném đá giết con mất!"

ko.L: 그러자 모세가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖어 말했다. "제가 이 백성에게 무엇을 해야 합니까? 조금만 더 있으면 그들이 저를 돌로 칠 것입니다."
ko.B: 모세가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. "제가 이 백성을 어떻게 해야 합니까? 조금만 더 지나면 이들이 저를 돌로 칠 것입니다!"
ko.R: 모세가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 부르짖었다. "이 사람들을 어떻게 하면 좋겠습니까? 이러다가는 곧 이 사람들이 저에게 돌을 던져 저를 죽이려고 할 것입니다!"

pt.L: E Moisés clamou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, dizendo: "Que farei com este povo? Mais um pouco e me apedrejarão."
pt.B: Moisés clamou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "O que vou fazer com este povo? Mais um pouco e eles me apedrejam!"
pt.R: Moisés clamou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. "O que devo fazer com este povo?", ele disse. "Daqui a pouco eles vão me matar a pedradas!"

decisions.choice: yet a little: very soon, almost
decisions.reason: The phrase means that only a little more is needed, or that only a little time remains, before they stone him.

decisions.choice: stone me: put me to death by stoning
decisions.reason: Stoning was a way a crowd or a community put someone to death (Numbers 14:10; 1 Samuel 30:6).

decisions.choice: throwing stones at me to kill me
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what stoning is.

decisions.choice: Moses speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "저"; God speaks to Moses in 해라체 with "나" and "너"
decisions.reason: As in Genesis: people speak to God in prayer forms, and God speaks in 해라체.

decisions.choice: Moses calls himself "con" when he speaks to the LORD
decisions.reason: The Genesis terms note has people praying say "con" and speak to God as "Ngài" or "Chúa"; Moses' cry here is a prayer. Recorded once for these chapters.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲבֹר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְקַ֥ח אִתְּךָ֖ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַטְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכִּ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיְאֹ֔ר קַ֥ח בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְהָלָֽכְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, pass on before the people and take with you some of [the] elders of Israel, and your staff with which you struck the River take in your hand and go.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Pass on before the people, and take with you [some] of the elders of Israel, and your staff with which you struck the River take in your hand, and go.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Walk on ahead of the people, and bring some of Israel's elders with you. Take along your staff, the one you struck the Nile with, hold it in your hand, and go.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "Go on ahead of the people. Bring some of the leaders of Israel with you. Carry the staff you used to strike the Nile River, and go.

es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Adelántate al pueblo y lleva contigo a algunos de los ancianos de Israel. Toma también tu vara, la misma con que golpeaste el Nilo; llévala en la mano y ve.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió a Moisés: «Ve delante del pueblo. Lleva contigo a algunos de los líderes de Israel. Toma la vara con la que golpeaste el río Nilo, y ve.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Passe devant le peuple, et prends avec toi [quelques-uns] des anciens d’Israël, et ton bâton, avec lequel tu as frappé le Fleuve, prends-le dans ta main, et va.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Avance devant le peuple, et emmène avec toi quelques anciens d’Israël. Prends aussi ton bâton, celui avec lequel tu as frappé le Nil ; tiens-le à la main, et va.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu à Moïse : « Va devant le peuple. Emmène avec toi quelques responsables d’Israël. Prends le bâton avec lequel tu as frappé le Nil, et va.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Pita mbele ya watu, ukachukue pamoja nawe [baadhi] ya wazee wa Israeli, na fimbo yako uliyoupiga nayo Mto, ishike mkononi mwako, uende.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Tangulia mbele ya watu, uwachukue baadhi ya wazee wa Israeli pamoja nawe. Chukua pia fimbo yako, ile uliyoupiga nayo mto Naili; ishike mkononi, uende.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu Musa, "Tangulia mbele ya watu. Wachukue baadhi ya viongozi wa Israeli pamoja nawe. Chukua fimbo uliyoupiga nayo Mto Naili, uende.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy đi qua trước mặt dân, và đem theo với ngươi [vài người] trong các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên; và cây gậy của ngươi, là cây gậy ngươi đã dùng đập Sông, hãy cầm trong tay ngươi mà đi.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Con hãy đi trước dân chúng và đem theo vài trưởng lão của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Hãy cầm trong tay cây gậy con đã dùng để đập sông Nin, rồi đi.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trả lời Môi-se: "Con hãy đi trước dân chúng. Đem theo vài người lãnh đạo của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Hãy cầm cây gậy con đã dùng để đánh sông Nin, rồi đi.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "백성 앞으로 지나가거라. 이스라엘의 장로들 가운데 [몇 사람을] 너와 함께 데리고, 네가 그것으로 강을 쳤던 네 지팡이를 네 손에 잡고 가거라.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "백성보다 앞서 걸어가거라. 이스라엘의 장로들 가운데 몇 사람을 데리고, 네가 나일강을 칠 때 썼던 그 지팡이를 손에 들고 가거라.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 대답하셨다. "백성보다 앞서 가거라. 이스라엘의 지도자들 몇 사람을 데리고 가거라. 네가 나일강을 쳤던 지팡이를 들고 가거라.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Passa adiante do povo, e leva contigo [alguns] dos anciãos de Israel, e o teu cajado, com que feriste o Rio, toma na tua mão, e vai.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Vai à frente do povo e leva contigo alguns dos anciãos de Israel. Leva também o teu cajado, aquele com que feriste o Nilo; segura-o na mão e vai.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu a Moisés: "Vai na frente do povo. Leva contigo alguns dos líderes de Israel. Leva o cajado que usaste para bater no rio Nilo, e vai.

decisions.choice: the staff with which you struck the River: the staff of the first plague
decisions.reason: Moses struck the water of the Nile with this staff, and it became blood (7:17, 20). The staff that brought death to Egypt's water will now bring water out of rock.

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the heads of the families and clans
decisions.reason: The elders were the older leaders of Israel's families (3:16; 12:21). Here they go as witnesses of what God does (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the Nile
decisions.reason: "The River" is the Nile, as everywhere in Exodus. Balanced and Readable name it; Literal keeps "the River".

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", as in 3:16 and 12:21.

decisions.choice: God calls Moses "ngươi" (L), "con" (B, R), and himself "Ta"
decisions.reason: The address the Genesis terms note settles for God speaking to a person: "ngươi" keeps the distance of the Hebrew at Literal, "con" the warmth of a father at Balanced and Readable. Recorded once for chapters 17 to 24; the laws spoken to the whole people keep "ngươi" / "các ngươi" at every level, as the term sheet sets.

decisions.choice: "Sông" (L); "sông Nin" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the River"; Literal keeps it with a capital, as the English Literal does, and Balanced and Readable name the Nile.

records.literal_gloss: Behold I [will be] standing before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you will strike the rock, and will come out from it water, and will drink the people. And did so Moses in [the] eyes of [the] elders of Israel.

en.L: Behold, I [will be] standing before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink." And Moses did so in the eyes of the elders of Israel.
en.B: Look, I will be standing there before you, on the rock at Horeb. You are to strike the rock, and water will pour out of it, and the people will drink." Moses did so, with the elders of Israel looking on.
en.R: I will be there in front of you, standing on the rock at Horeb. Hit the rock, and water will come out of it. Then the people will have water to drink." Moses did this while the leaders of Israel watched.

es.L: He aquí, yo estaré delante de ti allí sobre la roca en Horeb; y golpearás la roca, y saldrá agua de ella, y beberá el pueblo». E hizo así Moisés a los ojos de los ancianos de Israel.
es.B: Mira, yo estaré allí delante de ti, sobre la roca de Horeb. Tú golpearás la roca, y brotará agua de ella, y el pueblo beberá». Moisés lo hizo así, mientras los ancianos de Israel miraban.
es.R: Yo estaré allí delante de ti, de pie sobre la roca de Horeb. Golpea la roca, y saldrá agua. Entonces el pueblo tendrá agua para beber». Moisés lo hizo mientras los líderes de Israel lo miraban.

fr.L: Voici, je me tiendrai là devant toi sur le rocher, à l’Horeb ; et tu frapperas le rocher, et de l’eau en sortira, et le peuple boira. » Et Moïse fit ainsi sous les yeux des anciens d’Israël.
fr.B: Voici, je me tiendrai là devant toi, sur le rocher, à l’Horeb. Tu frapperas le rocher ; l’eau en jaillira et le peuple boira. » Moïse fit ainsi, sous le regard des anciens d’Israël.
fr.R: Je serai là devant toi, debout sur le rocher, à l’Horeb. Frappe le rocher, et de l’eau en sortira. Alors le peuple aura de l’eau à boire. » Moïse l’a fait, sous les yeux des responsables d’Israël.

sw.L: Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitasimama mbele yako huko juu ya mwamba katika Horebu; nawe utaupiga mwamba, na maji yatatoka ndani yake, nao watu watakunywa." Naye Musa akafanya hivyo machoni pa wazee wa Israeli.
sw.B: Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitasimama huko mbele yako, juu ya mwamba ulioko Horebu. Utaupiga mwamba, na maji yatabubujika kutoka ndani yake, nao watu watakunywa." Musa alifanya hivyo, wazee wa Israeli wakiwa wanatazama.
sw.R: Nitakuwa pale mbele yako, nimesimama juu ya mwamba huko Horebu. Piga mwamba huo, na maji yatatoka ndani yake. Ndipo watu watapata maji ya kunywa." Musa alifanya hivyo viongozi wa Israeli wakitazama.

vi.L: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đứng trước mặt ngươi tại đó, trên tảng đá ở Hô-rếp; và ngươi sẽ đập vào tảng đá, và nước sẽ chảy ra từ nó, và dân sẽ uống." Và Môi-se làm như vậy trước mắt các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đứng đó trước mặt con, trên tảng đá ở Hô-rếp. Con hãy đập vào tảng đá, nước sẽ từ đó tuôn ra, và dân chúng sẽ có nước uống." Môi-se làm như vậy trước mắt các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Ta sẽ ở đó trước mặt con, đứng trên tảng đá ở Hô-rếp. Con hãy đập vào tảng đá, rồi nước sẽ chảy ra. Như vậy dân chúng sẽ có nước uống." Môi-se làm như vậy trong khi các người lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên đứng xem.

ko.L: 보아라, 내가 거기 호렙에 있는 바위 위에서 네 앞에 서 있겠다. 너는 그 바위를 쳐라. 그러면 거기서 물이 나와 백성이 마실 것이다." 모세가 이스라엘 장로들의 눈앞에서 그렇게 했다.

decisions.choice: I will stand before you on the rock: God himself is present at the rock
alternatives: I will stand before you by the rock
decisions.reason: God says he will stand on or by the rock in front of Moses. The water comes because God is there, which answers the people's question in verse 7. Later Scripture calls God the Rock of his people (Deuteronomy 32:4, 15), and Paul says the rock that followed them was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4).

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain of God, also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Horeb is the mountain where God first met Moses (3:1). The water comes from the area of the mountain the people are coming to (19:1-2).

decisions.reason: At a later Meribah, God told Moses to speak to the rock, but Moses struck it twice and was kept out of the land (Numbers 20:7-12).

records.literal_gloss: And he called [the] name of the place Massah and Meribah, on account of [the] quarrel of [the] sons of Israel and because of their testing Yahweh, saying, is there Yahweh in our midst or not?

en.L: And he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the quarreling of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and because they tested {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in our midst or not?"
en.B: He named the place Massah, "testing," and Meribah, "quarreling," because there the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} quarreled, and there they put {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the test by asking, "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} among us or not?"
en.R: Moses named the place Massah, which means "testing," and Meribah, which means "arguing." He gave it these names because the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} argued there. They also tested {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by asking, "Is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with us or not?"

es.L: Y llamó el nombre del lugar Masá y Meribá, por la contienda de los hijos de Israel, y porque pusieron a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «¿Está {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} en medio de nosotros, o no?».
es.B: Puso a aquel lugar el nombre de Masá, «Prueba», y Meribá, «Contienda», porque allí los israelitas contendieron, y allí pusieron a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} al preguntar: «¿Está {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entre nosotros o no?».
es.R: Moisés llamó a aquel lugar Masá, que significa «prueba», y Meribá, que significa «discusión». Le puso esos nombres porque allí los israelitas discutieron. Además pusieron a prueba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} al preguntar: «¿Está {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} con nosotros o no?».

fr.L: Et il appela le nom du lieu Massa et Meriba, à cause de la querelle des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, et parce qu’ils avaient mis à l’épreuve {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en disant : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est-il au milieu de nous, ou non ? »
fr.B: Il donna à ce lieu le nom de Massa, « Épreuve », et de Meriba, « Querelle », parce que là les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} avaient cherché querelle, et que là ils avaient mis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à l’épreuve en demandant : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est-il au milieu de nous, oui ou non ? »
fr.R: Moïse a appelé ce lieu Massa, ce qui veut dire « mise à l’épreuve », et Meriba, ce qui veut dire « dispute ». Il lui a donné ces noms parce que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} s’y étaient disputés. Ils avaient aussi mis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à l’épreuve en demandant : « Est-ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec nous, oui ou non ? »

sw.L: Naye akapaita jina la mahali pale Masa na Meriba, kwa sababu ya ugomvi wa wana wa Israeli, na kwa sababu walimjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakisema, "Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko katikati yetu au hayuko?"
sw.B: Alipaita mahali pale Masa, "Kujaribu," na Meriba, "Ugomvi," kwa sababu huko Waisraeli waligombana, na huko walimjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa kuuliza, "Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko pamoja nasi au hayuko?"
sw.R: Musa alipaita mahali pale Masa, maana yake "kujaribu," na Meriba, maana yake "kubishana." Alipaita hivyo kwa sababu Waisraeli walibishana huko. Pia walimjaribu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa kuuliza, "Je, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko pamoja nasi au hayuko?"

vi.L: Và ông gọi tên chỗ ấy là Ma-sa và Mê-ri-ba, vì sự cãi vã của con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, và vì họ đã thử {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà rằng: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} có ở giữa chúng ta hay không?"
vi.B: Ông đặt tên nơi ấy là Ma-sa, nghĩa là "thử thách", và Mê-ri-ba, nghĩa là "cãi vã", vì tại đó dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã cãi vã, và tại đó họ đã thử thách {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} khi hỏi: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} có ở giữa chúng ta hay không?"
vi.R: Môi-se đặt tên nơi ấy là Ma-sa, nghĩa là "thử thách", và Mê-ri-ba, nghĩa là "cãi lẫy". Ông đặt những tên này vì dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã cãi lẫy tại đó. Họ cũng đã thử thách {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} khi hỏi: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} có ở với chúng ta hay không?"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 그곳의 이름을 맛사와 므리바라고 불렀다. 이스라엘 자손이 다투었기 때문이고, 그들이 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리 가운데 계시냐, 안 계시냐?" 하고 말하며 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 시험했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그는 그곳의 이름을 '시험'이라는 뜻의 맛사, '다툼'이라는 뜻의 므리바라고 지었다. 이스라엘 백성이 그곳에서 다투었고, "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리 가운데 계신가, 안 계신가?" 하고 물으며 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 시험했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 모세는 그곳을 맛사와 므리바라고 불렀다. 맛사는 '시험'이라는 뜻이고, 므리바는 '다툼'이라는 뜻이다. 이스라엘 사람들이 그곳에서 다투었기 때문이다. 그들은 또 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리와 함께 계시냐, 안 계시냐?" 하고 물으며 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 시험했다.

pt.L: E ele chamou o nome do lugar Massá e Meribá, por causa da contenda dos filhos de Israel e porque puseram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} à prova, dizendo: "Está {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} no meio de nós, ou não?"
pt.B: Ele deu ao lugar o nome de Massá, "prova", e Meribá, "disputa", porque ali os israelitas entraram em disputa e ali puseram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} à prova, perguntando: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} está conosco ou não?"
pt.R: Moisés deu ao lugar o nome de Massá, que quer dizer "prova", e Meribá, que quer dizer "discussão". Ele deu esses nomes porque ali os israelitas discutiram. Eles também puseram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} à prova, perguntando: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} está conosco ou não?"

decisions.choice: Massah and Meribah: "testing" and "quarreling"
decisions.reason: The two names are a play on the verbs of verse 2. Massah comes from the root "to test" and Meribah from the root "to quarrel". The place is named for what the people did there, not for the water.

decisions.choice: Is Yahweh among us or not?: the question at the heart of the testing
decisions.reason: After the plagues, the sea and the manna, the people still ask whether the LORD is with them. God's answer is to stand before them on the rock (verse 6).

decisions.choice: Massah and Meribah are remembered as a warning
decisions.reason: Psalm 95:8-9 names both places, warning God's people not to harden their hearts as their ancestors did when they tested God there. See also Deuteronomy 6:16; 33:8; Psalm 81:8; and Hebrews 3:7-11, which quotes Psalm 95.

decisions.choice: "testing" ... "quarreling" / which means
decisions.reason: The point of the names is lost unless the reader knows what they mean, so Balanced and Readable give the meanings. Literal keeps only the names.

decisions.choice: "Prueba" and "Contienda" (B), "prueba" and "discusión" (R) for the meanings of the names
decisions.reason: The meanings repeat the verbs of verse 2 at each level ("poner a prueba", "contender" at B, "discutir" at R), so the reader sees that the names come from what the people did.

decisions.choice: "Épreuve" and "Querelle" (B), "mise à l'épreuve" and "dispute" (R) for the meanings of the names
decisions.reason: The meanings repeat the words of verse 2 at each level ("mettre à l'épreuve", "chercher querelle" at B, "se disputer" at R), so the names are seen to come from what the people did.

decisions.choice: "Kujaribu" and "Ugomvi" (B), "kujaribu" and "kubishana" (R) for the meanings of the names
decisions.reason: The meanings repeat the verbs of verse 2 at each level ("kumjaribu", "kugombana" at B, "kubishana" at R), so the names are seen to come from what the people did.

decisions.choice: "맛사", "므리바"
decisions.reason: The names as the Korean Psalms already give them (Psalm 95:8; 81:8), so the place is recognized when the Psalms recall it.

decisions.choice: "Ma-sa" and "Mê-ri-ba"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant forms of the two names, kept for their later mentions (Numbers 20; Deuteronomy 6:16; Psalm 95:8). Balanced and Readable give their sense in quotation marks, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Massá e Meribá; "prova", "disputa" (B); "prova", "discussão" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "Massá" and "Meribá", the usual Brazilian forms, stressed on the last syllable, without the h Portuguese does not sound. Balanced and Readable give their meanings with the same words used for the verbs in verse 2, so that the play on the names (m1) can be heard.

decisions.choice: Amalek: a desert people descended from Esau
decisions.reason: Amalek was a grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:12). His descendants, the Amalekites, were a wandering people of the southern desert (Numbers 13:29). Deuteronomy 25:17-18 adds that they attacked the weary stragglers at the rear.

decisions.choice: the Amalekites / the army of Amalek

decisions.choice: Joshua: Moses' assistant, here named for the first time
decisions.reason: This is the first time Joshua appears. He becomes Moses' assistant (24:13; 33:11) and leads Israel into the land after Moses' death (Numbers 27:18-23; Joshua 1:1-2). His name means "Yahweh saves".

decisions.choice: the staff of God: Moses' staff, set apart for God's work
decisions.reason: Moses' own staff is called "the staff of God" in 4:20, since God works his signs through it.

decisions.choice: Moses speaks to Joshua in 해라체
decisions.reason: Joshua is Moses' assistant; the leader speaks to him as a master to his servant does in the Genesis sheet, and Joshua answers in 합쇼체 where he speaks.

decisions.choice: Moses says "tôi" to Joshua
decisions.reason: Joshua is Moses' younger assistant, but he is also the commander sent out to battle; "tôi" keeps Moses' words plain and respectful, without the master's "ta". A reviewer may prefer "ta" / "con".

decisions.choice: você (Moses to Joshua)
decisions.reason: Moses gives orders to his young assistant (m1) with "você", the ordinary form between people (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md); "tu" is kept for speech to and from God.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר אָֽמַר־לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בַּעֲמָלֵ֑ק וּמֹשֶׁה֙ אַהֲרֹ֣ן וְח֔וּר עָל֖וּ רֹ֥אשׁ הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And did Joshua as said to him Moses, to fight against Amalek, and Moses, Aaron and Hur went up [to the] top of the hill.

en.L: And Joshua did as Moses had said to him, fighting against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up [to the] top of the hill.
en.B: Joshua did what Moses had told him and fought Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur climbed to the top of the hill.
en.R: Joshua did what Moses said and fought the Amalekites. Meanwhile, Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

es.L: E hizo Josué como le había dicho Moisés, peleando contra Amalec; y Moisés, Aarón y Hur subieron [a la] cumbre de la colina.
es.B: Josué hizo lo que Moisés le había dicho y combatió contra Amalec, mientras Moisés, Aarón y Hur subían a la cima de la colina.
es.R: Josué hizo lo que Moisés le dijo y peleó contra los amalecitas. Mientras tanto, Moisés, Aarón y Hur subieron a lo alto de la colina.

fr.L: Et Josué fit comme Moïse lui avait dit, en combattant contre Amalek ; et Moïse, Aaron et Hour montèrent [au] sommet de la colline.
fr.B: Josué fit ce que Moïse lui avait dit et combattit Amalek, tandis que Moïse, Aaron et Hour montaient au sommet de la colline.
fr.R: Josué a fait ce que Moïse avait dit, et il a combattu les Amalécites. Pendant ce temps, Moïse, Aaron et Hour sont montés en haut de la colline.

sw.L: Naye Yoshua akafanya kama Musa alivyomwambia, akipigana na Amaleki; nao Musa, Haruni na Huri wakapanda [hadi] kilele cha kilima.
sw.B: Yoshua alifanya kama Musa alivyomwambia, akapigana na Amaleki, huku Musa, Haruni na Huri wakipanda juu ya kilele cha kilima.
sw.R: Yoshua alifanya kama Musa alivyosema, akapigana na Waamaleki. Wakati huo Musa, Haruni na Huri walipanda juu ya kilima.

vi.L: Và Giô-suê làm như Môi-se đã nói với ông, để giao chiến với A-ma-léc; còn Môi-se, A-rôn và Hu-rơ đi lên đỉnh đồi.
vi.B: Giô-suê làm theo lời Môi-se dặn và giao chiến với A-ma-léc, trong khi Môi-se, A-rôn và Hu-rơ leo lên đỉnh đồi.
vi.R: Giô-suê làm theo lời Môi-se và đánh quân A-ma-léc. Trong lúc đó, Môi-se, A-rôn và Hu-rơ đi lên đỉnh đồi.

ko.L: 여호수아는 모세가 그에게 말한 대로 하여 아말렉과 싸웠고, 모세와 아론과 훌은 언덕 꼭대기로 올라갔다.
ko.B: 여호수아는 모세가 말한 대로 아말렉과 싸웠고, 그동안 모세와 아론과 훌은 언덕 꼭대기에 올라갔다.
ko.R: 여호수아는 모세가 말한 대로 아말렉 사람들과 싸웠다. 그동안 모세와 아론과 훌은 언덕 꼭대기로 올라갔다.

pt.L: E Josué fez como Moisés lhe dissera, lutando contra Amaleque; e Moisés, Arão e Hur subiram ao alto da colina.
pt.B: Josué fez o que Moisés lhe tinha mandado e lutou contra Amaleque, enquanto Moisés, Arão e Hur subiram ao alto da colina.
pt.R: Josué fez o que Moisés disse e lutou contra os amalequitas. Enquanto isso, Moisés, Arão e Hur subiram ao alto da colina.

decisions.choice: Hur: a leader beside Aaron
decisions.reason: Hur appears again with Aaron as one left in charge while Moses is on the mountain (24:14). He may be the Hur of the tribe of Judah whose grandson Bezalel built the tabernacle (31:2), though the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: Hur
decisions.reason: For the whole book, where the name first appears: "Hur" is kept as it is spelled in Portuguese Bibles, though the h is not sounded.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥ים מֹשֶׁ֛ה יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָנִ֛יחַ יָד֖וֹ וְגָבַ֥ר עֲמָלֵֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when lifted up Moses his hand, and prevailed Israel, and when he let rest his hand, and prevailed Amalek.

en.L: And it was, when Moses lifted up his hand, Israel prevailed, and when he let his hand rest, Amalek prevailed.
en.B: Whenever Moses held his hand high, Israel prevailed; and whenever he let it sink, Amalek prevailed.
en.R: When Moses held his hand up, Israel was winning the battle. When he let it down, Amalek was winning.

es.L: Y sucedía que, cuando alzaba Moisés su mano, prevalecía Israel, y cuando dejaba descansar su mano, prevalecía Amalec.
es.B: Siempre que Moisés mantenía en alto la mano, Israel llevaba ventaja; y siempre que la dejaba caer, la llevaba Amalec.
es.R: Cuando Moisés tenía la mano levantada, Israel iba ganando la batalla. Cuando la bajaba, iba ganando Amalec.

fr.L: Et il arrivait, quand Moïse élevait sa main, qu’Israël l’emportait, et quand il laissait reposer sa main, Amalek l’emportait.
fr.B: Chaque fois que Moïse tenait la main levée, Israël l’emportait ; et chaque fois qu’il la laissait retomber, Amalek l’emportait.
fr.R: Quand Moïse tenait la main levée, c’était Israël qui gagnait la bataille. Quand il la baissait, c’était Amalek qui gagnait.

sw.L: Ikawa, Musa alipoinua mkono wake, Israeli akashinda, na alipouacha mkono wake upumzike, Amaleki akashinda.
sw.B: Kila Musa alipoushikilia mkono wake juu, Israeli walishinda; na kila alipoushusha, Amaleki walishinda.
sw.R: Musa alipoushika mkono wake juu, Waisraeli walikuwa wakishinda vita. Alipoushusha, Waamaleki walikuwa wakishinda.

vi.L: Và xảy ra, khi Môi-se giơ tay lên thì Y-sơ-ra-ên thắng thế, và khi ông buông tay xuống thì A-ma-léc thắng thế.
vi.B: Hễ Môi-se giơ tay lên thì Y-sơ-ra-ên thắng thế; còn hễ ông hạ tay xuống thì A-ma-léc thắng thế.
vi.R: Khi Môi-se giơ tay lên, quân Y-sơ-ra-ên thắng. Khi ông hạ tay xuống, quân A-ma-léc thắng.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 그의 손을 들면 이스라엘이 우세하였고, 그의 손을 내리면 아말렉이 우세하였다.
ko.B: 모세가 손을 높이 들고 있으면 이스라엘이 이겼고, 손을 내리면 아말렉이 이겼다.
ko.R: 모세가 손을 들고 있으면 이스라엘이 싸움에서 이기고 있었다. 그러나 손을 내리면 아말렉이 이기고 있었다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando Moisés levantava a sua mão, Israel prevalecia, e, quando ele abaixava a sua mão, Amaleque prevalecia.
pt.B: Sempre que Moisés mantinha a mão erguida, Israel levava a melhor; e sempre que a abaixava, Amaleque levava a melhor.
pt.R: Quando Moisés mantinha a mão levantada, Israel estava vencendo a batalha. Quando ele a abaixava, Amaleque estava vencendo.

decisions.choice: when Moses lifted his hand, Israel prevailed: the victory comes from God
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether the raised hand with the staff was a sign of God's power or a gesture of prayer. Either way, the battle turns not on Joshua's soldiers alone but on God, whose staff Moses holds up (verse 9; compare 14:16).

decisions.choice: his hand: singular in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text has "his hand" here, while verse 12 has "his hands". The Samaritan Pentateuch and some other early witnesses have the plural here as well. The sense is the same.

source.text: וִידֵ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ כְּבֵדִ֔ים וַיִּקְחוּ־אֶ֛בֶן וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ תַחְתָּ֖יו וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב עָלֶ֑יהָ וְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וְח֜וּר תָּֽמְכ֣וּ בְיָדָ֗יו מִזֶּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וּמִזֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י יָדָ֛יו אֱמוּנָ֖ה עַד־בֹּ֥א הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] hands of Moses [were] heavy, and they took a stone and put [it] under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, from this [side] one and from this [side] one; and were his hands steadiness until [the] going of the sun.

en.L: And the hands of Moses [were] heavy, and they took a stone and put [it] under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on this [side] and one on that [side]; and his hands were steadiness until the going [down] of the sun.
en.B: Moses' hands grew heavy, so they got a stone and set it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one of them on each side, and so his hands stayed firm until the sun set.
en.R: Moses' arms got tired. So Aaron and Hur found a stone for him to sit on. They stood on each side of him and held up his arms. They kept his arms up without wavering until the sun went down.

es.L: Y las manos de Moisés [estaban] pesadas, y tomaron una piedra y [la] pusieron debajo de él, y se sentó sobre ella; y Aarón y Hur sostenían sus manos, uno de este [lado] y otro de este [lado]; y fueron sus manos firmeza hasta la puesta del sol.
es.B: Las manos de Moisés se cansaron, así que tomaron una piedra, se la pusieron debajo y él se sentó en ella. Aarón y Hur le sostenían las manos, uno de cada lado, y así sus manos se mantuvieron firmes hasta que se puso el sol.
es.R: A Moisés se le cansaron los brazos. Entonces Aarón y Hur buscaron una piedra para que se sentara en ella. Se pusieron uno a cada lado y le sostuvieron los brazos en alto. Así los mantuvieron firmes, sin que se bajaran, hasta que se puso el sol.

fr.L: Et les mains de Moïse [étaient] lourdes ; et ils prirent une pierre et [la] mirent sous lui, et il s’assit dessus ; et Aaron et Hour soutenaient ses mains, l’un de ce [côté-ci] et l’un de ce [côté-là] ; et ses mains furent fermeté jusqu’au coucher du soleil.
fr.B: Les mains de Moïse s’alourdirent ; on prit donc une pierre qu’on plaça sous lui, et il s’assit dessus. Aaron et Hour lui soutenaient les mains, l’un d’un côté, l’autre de l’autre, et ainsi ses mains restèrent fermes jusqu’au coucher du soleil.
fr.R: Les bras de Moïse se sont fatigués. Alors Aaron et Hour ont trouvé une pierre pour qu’il s’assoie dessus. Ils se sont mis chacun d’un côté de lui et lui ont tenu les bras levés. Ils les ont gardés levés sans faiblir jusqu’au coucher du soleil.

sw.L: Nayo mikono ya Musa [ilikuwa] mizito; nao wakatwaa jiwe wakaliweka chini yake, naye akaketi juu yake; nao Haruni na Huri wakaitegemeza mikono yake, mmoja upande huu na mmoja upande huu; nayo mikono yake ikawa uthabiti hata kuchwa kwa jua.
sw.B: Mikono ya Musa ilipochoka, walichukua jiwe wakaliweka chini yake, naye akaketi juu yake. Haruni na Huri wakaishikilia mikono yake juu, mmoja upande huu na mwingine upande ule, hivyo mikono yake ikabaki imara mpaka jua lilipotua.
sw.R: Mikono ya Musa ilichoka. Basi Haruni na Huri walitafuta jiwe ili aketi juu yake. Walisimama kila mmoja upande wake, wakaishikilia mikono yake juu. Waliishikilia bila kulegea mpaka jua lilipotua.

vi.L: Và tay Môi-se nặng mỏi, và họ lấy một hòn đá đặt [nó] dưới ông, và ông ngồi lên trên; còn A-rôn và Hu-rơ đỡ tay ông, một người bên này và một người bên kia; và tay ông vững vàng cho đến khi mặt trời lặn.
vi.B: Tay Môi-se mỏi dần, nên họ lấy một hòn đá đặt dưới ông, và ông ngồi lên đó. A-rôn và Hu-rơ đỡ tay ông, mỗi người một bên, nhờ vậy tay ông vẫn vững cho đến khi mặt trời lặn.
vi.R: Tay Môi-se mỏi. Vì vậy A-rôn và Hu-rơ tìm một hòn đá cho ông ngồi. Họ đứng hai bên ông và đỡ tay ông lên. Họ giữ tay ông vững vàng cho đến khi mặt trời lặn.

ko.L: 그런데 모세의 손이 무거웠다. 그래서 그들이 돌 하나를 가져다가 그의 아래에 놓았고, 그가 그 위에 앉았다. 그리고 아론과 훌이 한 사람은 이쪽에서, 한 사람은 저쪽에서 그의 손을 붙들었다. 그래서 그의 손이 해가 질 때까지 굳건하였다.
ko.B: 모세의 손이 무거워지자, 그들은 돌을 가져다가 그의 밑에 놓았고, 모세는 그 위에 앉았다. 아론과 훌이 양쪽에서 한 사람씩 그의 손을 붙들어 올렸다. 그래서 그의 손은 해가 질 때까지 흔들림 없이 들려 있었다.
ko.R: 모세는 팔이 아파 왔다. 그래서 아론과 훌이 돌을 가져다 놓아 모세가 그 위에 앉게 했다. 두 사람은 모세의 양쪽에 서서 그의 팔을 붙들어 올렸다. 그들은 해가 질 때까지 모세의 팔이 흔들리지 않게 받쳐 주었다.

pt.L: E as mãos de Moisés [estavam] pesadas, e pegaram uma pedra e [a] puseram debaixo dele, e ele se sentou sobre ela; e Arão e Hur sustentavam as suas mãos, um deste [lado] e outro daquele [lado]; e as suas mãos foram firmeza até o pôr do sol.
pt.B: As mãos de Moisés ficaram pesadas. Então pegaram uma pedra e a puseram debaixo dele, e ele se sentou nela. Arão e Hur sustentavam as mãos dele, um de cada lado, e assim as suas mãos permaneceram firmes até o pôr do sol.
pt.R: Os braços de Moisés ficaram cansados. Então Arão e Hur encontraram uma pedra para ele se sentar. Eles ficaram um de cada lado e seguraram os braços dele para cima. Eles mantiveram os braços de Moisés firmes, sem baixar, até o sol se pôr.

decisions.choice: steady: firm, held fast, faithful
decisions.reason: The noun means firmness or steadiness, from the root behind "amen". Elsewhere the same noun is usually "faithfulness": of God (Deuteronomy 32:4; Lamentations 3:23) and of the righteous, who "live by faithfulness" (Habakkuk 2:4). Here it is Moses' hands that stay firm, held up by his helpers until the battle is won.

decisions.choice: heavy: tired, weighed down
decisions.reason: "Heavy" is the same word used of Pharaoh's heart (7:14). Here it means that Moses' arms grew tired from being held up.

decisions.choice: arms
decisions.reason: Holding the hands up means holding the arms up, and it is the arms that tire. Readable says "arms"; Literal and Balanced keep "hands".

decisions.choice: Aaron and Hur found a stone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they took a stone"; Readable names Aaron and Hur, who are the ones beside him.

decisions.choice: "mikono" at Readable too, where the English Readable says "arms"
alternatives: "mikono" at Literal and Balanced, another word at Readable
decisions.reason: Swahili "mkono" means both the hand and the whole arm, so the one word serves at every level and the change the English Readable makes is not needed.

decisions.choice: "vững vàng" (L, R); "vững" (B) for the hands that were "steadiness"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew noun means firmness, faithfulness (meaning decision); Vietnamese says it with the adjective, which keeps both the steady arms and the faithfulness.

records.literal_gloss: And overwhelmed Joshua Amalek and his people with [the] mouth of [the] sword.

en.L: And Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people with the mouth of the sword.
en.B: So Joshua cut down Amalek and its fighting men with the edge of the sword.
en.R: So Joshua and his soldiers used their swords to defeat the army of Amalek.

es.L: Y Josué abatió a Amalec y a su pueblo a boca de espada.
es.B: Así Josué derrotó a Amalec y a sus guerreros a filo de espada.
es.R: Así, Josué y sus soldados vencieron al ejército de Amalec con sus espadas.

fr.L: Et Josué terrassa Amalek et son peuple par la bouche de l’épée.
fr.B: Ainsi Josué abattit Amalek et ses combattants au tranchant de l’épée.
fr.R: Ainsi, Josué et ses soldats ont vaincu l’armée d’Amalek avec leurs épées.

sw.L: Naye Yoshua akamwangusha Amaleki na watu wake kwa kinywa cha upanga.
sw.B: Hivyo Yoshua aliwaangusha Amaleki na wapiganaji wake kwa makali ya upanga.
sw.R: Hivyo Yoshua na askari wake walilishinda jeshi la Amaleki kwa panga zao.

vi.L: Và Giô-suê đánh bại A-ma-léc và dân của nó bằng miệng gươm.
vi.B: Vậy Giô-suê dùng lưỡi gươm đánh bại A-ma-léc và quân của nó.
vi.R: Vậy Giô-suê và quân lính của ông dùng gươm đánh bại quân A-ma-léc.

ko.L: 그리고 여호수아가 아말렉과 그의 백성을 칼의 입으로 쳐서 무너뜨렸다.
ko.B: 그리하여 여호수아는 칼날로 아말렉과 그 군사들을 쳐서 무찔렀다.
ko.R: 여호수아와 그의 군사들은 칼로 아말렉 군대를 물리쳤다.

pt.L: E Josué abateu Amaleque e o seu povo com a boca da espada.
pt.B: Assim Josué derrotou Amaleque e os seus guerreiros a fio de espada.
pt.R: Assim Josué e os seus soldados usaram as suas espadas e derrotaram o exército de Amaleque.

decisions.choice: overwhelmed: laid low, defeated
decisions.reason: The verb means to weaken or bring down. It is used of a crushing defeat (Isaiah 14:12). It need not mean that every Amalekite was killed; they remain Israel's enemy (verse 16; 1 Samuel 15).

decisions.choice: the mouth of the sword: the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: The edge of a sword is pictured as a mouth that devours. The phrase means by force of arms in battle (Genesis 34:26; Joshua 6:21).

decisions.choice: his people: Amalek's fighting men
decisions.reason: "People" here are those who fought with Amalek, his troops.

decisions.choice: Joshua and his soldiers
decisions.reason: Joshua did not fight alone; he led the men he chose (verse 9). Readable says so.

decisions.choice: "칼의 입으로" (L); "칼날로" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture as the English Literal does; Balanced uses the ordinary Korean word for the edge of a sword.

decisions.choice: "miệng gươm" (L); "lưỡi gươm" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the sword's mouth (meaning decision); Balanced says "lưỡi gươm", the edge, the ordinary Vietnamese.

decisions.choice: com a boca da espada (L); a fio de espada (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the sword's "mouth" (m2), as the English Literal does. Balanced uses "a fio de espada", the Portuguese idiom for the same thing, the edge of the sword.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה כְּתֹ֨ב זֹ֤את זִכָּרוֹן֙ בַּסֵּ֔פֶר וְשִׂ֖ים בְּאָזְנֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ כִּֽי־מָחֹ֤ה אֶמְחֶה֙ אֶת־זֵ֣כֶר עֲמָלֵ֔ק מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, write this [as] a memorial in the book and put [it] in [the] ears of Joshua, that utterly I will blot out [the] remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Write this [as] a memorial in the book, and put [it] in the ears of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens."
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Record this in a scroll to be remembered, and say it over to Joshua: I will wipe out the memory of Amalek completely from under the heavens."
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Write this down on a scroll so it will be remembered, and read it out to Joshua: I will wipe out Amalek so completely that no one under heaven will remember them."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés: «Escribe esto [como] memorial en el libro, y pon[lo] en los oídos de Josué: que borraré del todo la memoria de Amalec de debajo de los cielos».
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Deja esto por escrito en un rollo para que se recuerde, y repíteselo a Josué: yo borraré por completo el recuerdo de Amalec de debajo del cielo».
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Escribe esto en un rollo para que se recuerde, y léeselo a Josué: voy a hacer desaparecer a Amalec tan completamente que nadie bajo el cielo se acordará de ellos».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Écris ceci [comme] mémorial dans le livre, et mets-[le] dans les oreilles de Josué, que j’effacerai entièrement le souvenir d’Amalek de dessous les cieux. »
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Mets cela par écrit dans un rouleau, pour qu’on s’en souvienne, et répète-le à Josué : j’effacerai complètement le souvenir d’Amalek de dessous les cieux. »
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Écris cela sur un rouleau pour qu’on s’en souvienne, et lis-le à Josué : je vais faire disparaître Amalek si complètement que plus personne sous le ciel ne se souviendra de lui. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Andika hili [kuwa] ukumbusho katika kitabu, ukalitie katika masikio ya Yoshua, ya kwamba hakika nitaifuta kabisa kumbukumbu ya Amaleki chini ya mbingu."
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Liandike jambo hili katika gombo ili likumbukwe, umwambie Yoshua maneno haya: nitaifuta kabisa kumbukumbu ya Amaleki chini ya mbingu."
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Andika jambo hili katika gombo ili likumbukwe, kisha umsomee Yoshua: nitawafuta Waamaleki kabisa hata mtu yeyote chini ya mbingu asiwakumbuke tena."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy chép điều này [làm] kỷ niệm vào sách, và đặt [nó] vào tai Giô-suê, rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xóa sạch kỷ niệm về A-ma-léc khỏi dưới trời."
vi.B: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy ghi việc này vào cuộn sách để ghi nhớ, và đọc lại cho Giô-suê nghe: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xóa sạch ký ức về A-ma-léc khỏi dưới bầu trời."
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy viết việc này vào một cuộn sách để người ta nhớ, và đọc cho Giô-suê nghe: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ diệt A-ma-léc đến nỗi dưới bầu trời này không còn ai nhớ đến chúng nữa."

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "이것을 기념으로 책에 기록하고 여호수아의 귀에 들려주어라. 내가 아말렉에 대한 기억을 하늘 아래에서 반드시 지워 버릴 것이기 때문이다."
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "이 일을 두루마리에 기록하여 기억하게 하고, 여호수아에게 똑똑히 들려주어라. 내가 아말렉에 대한 기억을 하늘 아래에서 완전히 지워 버리겠다."
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "이 일을 두루마리에 적어 사람들이 기억하게 하여라. 그리고 그것을 여호수아에게 읽어 주어라. 내가 아말렉을 완전히 없애서, 하늘 아래 그 누구도 그들을 기억하지 못하게 하겠다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Escreve isto [como] memorial no livro, e põe[-no] nos ouvidos de Josué: que eu apagarei completamente a lembrança de Amaleque de debaixo dos céus."
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Registra isto num rolo, para que seja lembrado, e repete-o a Josué: eu vou apagar por completo a memória de Amaleque de debaixo do céu."
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Moisés: "Escreve isto num rolo, para que seja lembrado, e lê em voz alta para Josué: eu vou destruir Amaleque tão completamente que ninguém debaixo do céu vai se lembrar dele."

decisions.choice: write in the book: the first time Moses is told to write
decisions.reason: This is the first time in the Bible that Moses is told to write something down (compare 24:4; 34:27; Numbers 33:2). A "book" was a scroll. The article may point to a known record, such as "the Book of the Wars of the LORD" (Numbers 21:14), or simply mean a scroll.

decisions.choice: put it in the ears of Joshua: make sure Joshua hears it
decisions.reason: To "put in the ears" is to tell someone so that they keep it in mind. Joshua will lead the people after Moses and must carry on the task.

decisions.choice: I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek
alternatives: for I will utterly blot out
decisions.reason: The doubled verb makes the promise emphatic. Deuteronomy 25:17-19 repeats the charge to Israel, and 1 Samuel 15 tells how Saul was sent against Amalek. The word "that" may also be read as "for": write it, because God will blot out Amalek.

decisions.choice: scroll
decisions.reason: Books in Moses' day were written on scrolls, so Balanced and Readable say "scroll"; Literal keeps "the book".

decisions.choice: "kỷ niệm" for both the memorial and the remembrance (L); "để ghi nhớ" and "ký ức" (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one root for the written memorial and the memory to be blotted out; Literal keeps one Vietnamese word for both, Balanced says each the plain way.

en.R: Moses built an altar there. He named it "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Is My Banner."

es.R: Moisés construyó un altar allí. Lo llamó «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es mi estandarte».

vi.L: Và Môi-se xây một bàn thờ và gọi tên nó là "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [Là] Ngọn Cờ Của Tôi".
vi.B: Rồi Môi-se xây một bàn thờ tại đó và đặt tên là "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Là Ngọn Cờ Của Tôi".
vi.R: Môi-se xây một bàn thờ tại đó. Ông đặt tên bàn thờ là "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Là Ngọn Cờ Của Tôi".

ko.L: 모세가 제단을 쌓고 그 이름을 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 나의 깃발"이라고 불렀다.
ko.B: 모세는 그곳에 제단을 쌓고, 그 이름을 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 나의 깃발"이라고 지었다.
ko.R: 모세는 그곳에 제단을 쌓았다. 그리고 그 제단을 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 나의 깃발"이라고 불렀다.

pt.L: E Moisés construiu um altar e lhe deu o nome "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} [É] a Minha Bandeira".
pt.B: Então Moisés construiu ali um altar e lhe deu o nome "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} É a Minha Bandeira".
pt.R: Moisés construiu ali um altar. Ele lhe deu o nome "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} É a Minha Bandeira".

decisions.choice: Yahweh is my banner: the LORD is the standard Israel rallies to
decisions.reason: A banner was a pole or standard raised high so that people could see it and gather to it, as for battle (Isaiah 5:26; 11:10, 12). In the altar's name the LORD himself is the standard under which Israel fought and won. The word may also echo the staff Moses held up on the hill (verses 9-12).

decisions.choice: built an altar and named it: an altar as a memorial
decisions.reason: Like the patriarchs, Moses gives the altar a name that tells what God has done (Genesis 33:20; 35:7; compare Genesis 22:14).

decisions.choice: "the LORD" inside the name
decisions.reason: The name of the altar contains the divine name, so it follows the reader's choice of "the LORD" or "Yahweh" like every other use of the name.

decisions.choice: "estandarte" for the banner
decisions.reason: "Estandarte" is a standard raised on a pole for troops to rally to, which is what the meaning decision describes; "bandera" today suggests a national flag.

decisions.choice: The altar's name translated, "주는 나의 깃발"
decisions.reason: The name is translated as the English translates it, so its sense is plain; the transliteration "여호와 닛시" known from older Korean Bibles is noted here for readers who look for it.

decisions.choice: "Ngọn Cờ" for the banner, and the name in capitals
decisions.reason: A banner is the standard troops gather around (meaning decision); "ngọn cờ" is that picture in Vietnamese. Each word of the altar's name is capitalised, as Vietnamese writes a proper name.

decisions.choice: "O SENHOR É a Minha Bandeira"
decisions.reason: The altar's name is translated, as in the English, and written with capitals as a name. "Bandeira" is the ordinary word for a banner raised for people to rally to (m1); "estandarte" is military and literary. The name follows the divine name setting like every other use of the name (r-en-1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־יָד֙ עַל־כֵּ֣ס יָ֔הּ מִלְחָמָ֥ה לַיהוָ֖ה בַּֽעֲמָלֵ֑ק מִדֹּ֖ר דֹּֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he said, for a hand upon [the] throne of Yah, war [belongs] to Yahweh with Amalek from generation [to] generation.

en.L: And he said, "For a hand [is] upon the throne of Yah! War [is] for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with Amalek from generation to generation."
en.B: He said, "A hand is lifted to the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fight Amalek generation after generation."
en.R: He said, "A hand is raised toward the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep fighting against Amalek in every generation."

es.L: Y dijo: «¡Porque una mano [está] sobre el trono de Yah! Guerra [tiene] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} con Amalec de generación en generación».
es.B: Dijo: «¡Una mano se alza hacia el trono {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yah}}! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} combatirá a Amalec de generación en generación».
es.R: Dijo: «¡Una mano se levanta hacia el trono {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yah}}! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} seguirá peleando contra Amalec en cada generación».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Car une main [est] sur le trône de Yah ! La guerre [est] pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} contre Amalek de génération en génération. »
fr.B: Il dit : « Une main s’est levée vers le trône {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yah}} ! {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera la guerre à Amalek de génération en génération. »
fr.R: Il a dit : « Une main est levée vers le trône {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yah}} ! {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} continuera à combattre Amalek à chaque génération. »

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Kwa maana mkono [u] juu ya kiti cha enzi cha Yah! Vita [ni] vya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} juu ya Amaleki kizazi hata kizazi."
sw.B: Akasema, "Mkono umeinuliwa kuelekea kiti cha enzi cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atapigana na Amaleki kizazi baada ya kizazi."
sw.R: Alisema, "Mkono umeinuliwa kuelekea kiti cha enzi cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yah}}! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ataendelea kupigana na Amaleki katika kila kizazi."

vi.L: Và ông nói: "Vì một bàn tay [ở] trên ngai của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia}}! Chiến tranh [thuộc về] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} với A-ma-léc từ đời nọ đến đời kia."
vi.B: Ông nói: "Một bàn tay giơ lên hướng về ngai của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia}}! {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ chiến đấu với A-ma-léc đời này qua đời khác."
vi.R: Ông nói: "Một bàn tay giơ lên hướng về ngai của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia}}! {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ tiếp tục chiến đấu chống lại A-ma-léc trong mọi thế hệ."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "참으로 손이 {{divine_name:주|야}}의 보좌 위에 [있다]! {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께는 대대로 아말렉과의 전쟁이 [있다]."
ko.B: 그가 말했다. "손이 {{divine_name:주|야}}의 보좌를 향하여 들렸다! {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대대로 아말렉과 싸우실 것이다."
ko.R: 그가 말했다. "손을 {{divine_name:주|야}}의 보좌를 향해 들었다! {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 대대로 아말렉과 계속 싸우실 것이다."

pt.L: E ele disse: "Pois uma mão [está] sobre o trono de Iá! Guerra [haverá] {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} contra Amaleque de geração em geração."
pt.B: Ele disse: "Uma mão se ergueu para o trono {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Iá}}! {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vai lutar contra Amaleque de geração em geração."
pt.R: Ele disse: "Uma mão está levantada para o trono {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Iá}}! {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vai continuar lutando contra Amaleque em todas as gerações."

decisions.choice: a hand upon the throne of Yah: very uncertain
alternatives: a hand raised against the throne of Yah
a hand upon the banner of Yah
decisions.reason: The words are short and hard to read. They may mean (1) a hand raised to God's throne in an oath, as God swears to fight Amalek; (2) a hand raised against God's throne, meaning that Amalek attacked the LORD's people and so the LORD himself; or (3), if the rare word "throne" is read as "banner" by a change of one letter, "a hand upon the banner of Yah", linking the saying to the altar's name in verse 15. The translation keeps the picture of the hand and the throne without deciding between these.

decisions.choice: Yah: a short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a short form of the name Yahweh, used in poetry and worship (15:2; Psalm 68:5; "hallelu-jah", "praise Yah").

decisions.choice: war for Yahweh with Amalek from generation to generation: an enmity that lasts
decisions.reason: The LORD's war against Amalek goes on age after age (1 Samuel 15:2-3; 30:1-18; 1 Chronicles 4:43).

decisions.choice: the LORD (Yah)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable treat the short name like the full one, with "Yah" as the alternative. Literal keeps "Yah" so the reader can see the shorter form.

decisions.choice: lifted to / raised toward
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "upon", "to" or "against". "Lifted to" keeps both the oath and the attack readings open. Literal keeps "upon".

decisions.choice: "Yah" as {{divine_name:주|야}} at every level
alternatives: plain "야" at Literal, as the English Literal has plain "Yah"
decisions.reason: The Korean Psalms write the short form of the name with this span; a bare "야" would read in Korean as an exclamation.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia}} for the short form Yah
decisions.reason: As the Vietnamese Psalms write Yah: the same default as the full name, with "Gia" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: Iá (L); {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Iá}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 15:2, the short form of the name is written "Iá". Literal keeps it plainly, as the English Literal keeps "Yah"; Balanced and Readable show it as "SENHOR" with "Iá" under the setting (r-en-1).
